planes.label: AUDIO
planes.description: mic capture, playback, DSP, onset and pitch detection (native audio thread)

planes.label: SYNC
planes.description: shared clock, latency compensation, event stream (lock-free)

planes.label: MOTION
planes.description: animation drivers, scenes and rendering (UI thread + GPU)

planes.label: SHARED
planes.description: types, utilities and music-theory tables usable from any thread

planes.label: PLATFORM
planes.description: iOS and Android projects and native modules

planes.label: APP
planes.description: screens, navigation, lessons, scoring, progress, storage (JS thread)

modules.name: App.tsx
modules.purpose: Root component: safe-area provider, hidden status bar, and the two screens: calibration first (every launch), then the lesson with real-time acoustic pitch detection.

modules.name: android
modules.purpose: Android app project: Gradle build, MainActivity, manifest and native Android code

modules.name: index.js
modules.purpose: Native entry point: registers the root App component with React Native.

modules.name: ios
modules.purpose: iOS app project: Xcode project, AppDelegate, Info.plist and native iOS code

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster
modules.purpose: The piano's single source of truth on screen, in three parts: CorePiano (the keyboard, any range: 48 keys by default, 88, 108 or any other), CoreNotes (the sheet music above it), and CorePianoNotesDetection (real-time acoustic pitch detection). Also owns the key state (which keys are lit, in which role) that lessons and the mic write to on the UI thread.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CoreNotes
modules.purpose: The sheet music above the piano, drawn with Skia and SMuFL music fonts: the music symbols (one folder each under symbols/), the score that places notes and rests on the staff, and the lesson design's own parts (staff paper, duration bars, playhead).

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CoreNotes/DurationBar
modules.purpose: The duration bar: the see-through bar after a note showing how long to hold it. Part of the lesson design, not a music symbol.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CoreNotes/Playhead
modules.purpose: The playhead: the big see-through vertical line marking where the music is now. Part of the lesson design, not a music symbol.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CoreNotes/StaffPaper
modules.purpose: The white paper strip behind the staff, with its soft shadow: part of the lesson design, not a music symbol.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CoreNotes/symbols
modules.purpose: The music notation symbols, one folder each and named as in music: Staff (the 5 lines), SystemicBarline, Barline, TrebleClef, TimeSignature, Notehead, Stem, LedgerLine, QuarterNote (notehead + stem) and QuarterRest. Each draws on its own, to be reused by any component.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CoreNotes/symbols/Barline
modules.purpose: The single barline: the vertical line that separates two measures.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CoreNotes/symbols/LedgerLine
modules.purpose: The ledger line: the short line through or under a notehead above or below the staff, such as middle C on a treble staff.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CoreNotes/symbols/Notehead
modules.purpose: The notehead: the filled oval of a note, centred on the note's line or space, and where a stem meets it.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CoreNotes/symbols/QuarterNote
modules.purpose: The quarter note: a notehead and a stem, with ledger lines when it sits above or below the staff; drawn in ink, or see-through red when it is the note to play now.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CoreNotes/symbols/QuarterRest
modules.purpose: The quarter rest: one beat of silence, on the middle line of the staff.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CoreNotes/symbols/Staff
modules.purpose: The staff: the 5 horizontal lines music is written on, and how far they reach.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CoreNotes/symbols/Stem
modules.purpose: The stem: the vertical line attached to a notehead.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CoreNotes/symbols/SystemicBarline
modules.purpose: The systemic barline: the vertical line at the very start of the staff.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CoreNotes/symbols/TimeSignature
modules.purpose: The time signature: the two stacked numbers at the start of the staff, beats per measure over the beat's note value (as in 4/4).

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CoreNotes/symbols/TrebleClef
modules.purpose: The treble clef (G clef): the sign at the start of the staff that fixes line 2 as G4.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CorePiano
modules.purpose: The piano keyboard at the bottom of PianoMaster: draws any range with Skia from one WhitePianoKey and one BlackPianoKey reused at every position, with the keybed, shadows, marker dots, note names and lit keys.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CorePiano/BlackPianoKey
modules.purpose: The one black piano key: how it looks at rest and when lit. CorePiano draws it at every black key position.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CorePiano/BlackPianoKeyShadows
modules.purpose: The shadows the black piano keys cast on the white keys, drawn for all black keys in one blurred layer.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CorePiano/PianoFrameShadow
modules.purpose: The shadow the keyboard frame casts across the top of the white piano keys.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CorePiano/PianoKeyLabel
modules.purpose: Note names on the piano keys: which keys show one and where (pure), and the system text that draws each name.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CorePiano/PianoKeyMarker
modules.purpose: The dot under a marked piano key, such as middle C.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CorePiano/PianoKeybed
modules.purpose: The keybed under the piano keys: the colour that shows through the gaps between the keys and the frame around them.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CorePiano/WhitePianoKey
modules.purpose: The one white piano key: how it looks at rest and when lit. CorePiano draws it at every white key position.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/CorePianoNotesDetection
modules.purpose: Acoustic note detection: the C++ engine (mic, pitch, calibration) and its bridge to PianoMaster. Detected keys light CorePiano from a lock-free native key table read on the UI thread; JS listeners get every note in order; the calibration guide says what to play.

modules.name: motion/scenes/PianoMaster/shared
modules.purpose: What more than one part of PianoMaster uses: the key state (which keys are lit, in which role), the lit-key colours, the key shape, gradients, paint helpers, picture recording and the look units; and for the music symbols, SMuFL glyph drawing, staff line positions and the notation ink.

modules.name: screens/CalibrationScreen
modules.purpose: The calibration screen shown at every launch: the lesson's layout with the questions on its white paper and the user's keyboard below, lighting the key to play and checking each strike; Save goes on to the lesson.

modules.name: screens/LessonScreen
modules.purpose: The lesson screen: background, top bar, staff and keyboard laid out exactly as the reference design, full screen in landscape.

modules.name: screens/game/EggHatch
modules.purpose: The egg-hatch screen: a paper-cut night forest where seven note ghosts (C D E F G A B) orbit an enchanted egg, crack it right where they strike, and a chick hatches in a burst of god light. Every scene element is its own atom under entities/; drawn with React Native Skia v3 + Reanimated 4.

modules.name: shared/piano
modules.purpose: The piano model: notes, MIDI numbers, frequencies, keyboards of any size and key positions. Pure code, usable from any thread.

modules.name: shared/typography
modules.purpose: The system fonts (SF Pro and SF Pro Rounded) and their metrics, so text can be placed by its baseline. React Native font family for SF Pro Rounded on iOS.

rules.description: Screens never touch audio internals or native modules.
Features and audio are imported only through their public index.ts.
Motion code may not import features, screens, state stores or audio; it uses other motion code, sync/ and shared/.
Audio code has no UI imports.
Code that runs every frame in motion never hands work back to the JS thread.
Motion code takes durations and easing from tokens, not hard-coded numbers.
Code on the UI or audio thread never imports JS-thread code.
